task:
The JWK Set cache of PyJWKClient cannot hold a parsed key set, and malformed key sets fail with the wrong errors. Fix all of these.

Pre-populating the cache fails. After client = PyJWKClient(url) and client.jwk_set_cache.put(PyJWKSet.from_dict(data)), client.get_jwk_set() raises PyJWKClientError("The JWKS endpoint did not return a JSON object"), though no endpoint was called. It must return that PyJWKSet without any network call, and jwk_set[kid].key_id must work on it.

The cache must always hold a parsed set. After a fetch through client.get_jwk_set(), client.jwk_set_cache.get() must be a PyJWKSet, and it must be the very object that get_jwk_set() returned (an `is` check). A second get_jwk_set() must return that same object with no network call.

The cached value must be the one that get_jwk_set() returned. A subclass may override fetch_data(), call super().fetch_data(), and return a dict with some keys filtered out. The first get_jwk_set() returns the filtered set. A second call must hit the cache, with no network call, and must return the same filtered keys. Today a removed key comes back.

JWKSetCache, from jwt.jwk_set_cache, takes a lifespan. Its put() must accept a PyJWKSet or a raw JWKS dict, and must store the dict parsed, so get() returns a PyJWKSet. put(None) must clear the cache, so get() returns None. Any other value, such as put("not a jwk set"), must raise PyJWKSetError with the message "Invalid JWK Set value".

When the endpoint returns JSON that is not an object, such as [{"kty": "RSA"}], get_jwk_set() must raise PyJWKClientError with "did not return a JSON object" in the message, with the cache enabled as it is by default.

PyJWKSet.from_dict raises an uncaught AttributeError on a member that is not an object. Such members must be skipped: {"keys": [None, "nope", 7, good_key]} must give a set that holds only good_key. {"keys": [None]} has no usable keys, so it must raise PyJWKSetError.

A JWK with a wrongly typed component raises an uncaught TypeError. PyJWK({"kty": "RSA", "alg": "RS256", "n": 1, "e": "AQAB"}) must raise InvalidKeyError. PyJWKSet.from_dict({"keys": [{"kty": "RSA", "n": 1, "e": "AQAB"}]}) must raise PyJWKSetError.

Everything else must keep working.
